title: Callfall resolver: runtime best-effort mapping of OpenAI-style tool calls to legacy function signatures with confidence metadata
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers are using both OpenAI-style tool descriptors (name/description/parameters JSON Schema) and an older, internal 'legacy function' surface (positional args, legacy param names, different casing). When a hosted Redwood runtime receives a tool call shaped like OpenAI tooling, downstream Dedicated/Private runtimes or older integrations sometimes fail due to naming/shape mismatches. We need a runtime-level best-effort resolver that maps incoming tool invocations to the legacy function surface without breaking streaming semantics or structured outputs.

Goal: Implement a Callfall resolver layer in the runtime that attempts non-destructive, observable mappings from OpenAI-style tool calls to legacy function signatures. The resolver should: (1) produce a deterministic mapping when confidence is high, (2) attach confidence/provenance metadata for low-confidence fallthroughs, (3) emit telemetry for ambiguous mappings and user-visible warnings when appropriate, (4) be toggleable per-customer or per-route, and (5) preserve streaming function-call semantics (e.g., partial tool-call payloads during chunked responses).

Key constraints: mappings must be reversible where possible (so we can include canonical names in logs), must never silently mutate arguments that could cause data loss (we prefer to include additional metadata rather than drop fields), and must minimize latency impact (prefer O(1) or small O(n) mappings using in-memory alias tables and compiled matchers).
acceptance_criteria: Resolver returns a mapping decision object for every incoming tool-call: {target_key, mapping_strategy, confidence_score, provenance_tags} (exposed as headers/metadata).
High-confidence mappings (confidence >= 0.9) are applied automatically without customer intervention and do not require additional runtime flags.
Low-confidence mappings attach x-rw-tool-confidence and x-rw-tool-provenance headers and route to a fallback path if configured (noop or runtime error depending on route configuration).

Streaming call flows preserve partial tool payloads: if a function call is emitted mid-stream, the resolver must not block streaming and must provide mapping metadata in the same stream/event sequence.

End-to-end integration tests cover name aliasing, positional->named param coercion, schema relaxation for missing optional fields, and explicit failure modes when required parameters are missing after coercion.
Telemetry: we record mapping outcome, confidence, latency impact, and downstream error rate to a new metric callfall.mapping.* and dashboards are created in Console-TOOL-RESOLVE.
Feature is behind a runtime toggle and opt-in per customer; rollout plan with canary for 5% / 25% / 100%.
Performance: median resolution latency added by resolver <= 1.5ms at p95 with a 32k alias table in-memory.
Documentation: PRD + runtime docs updated and a migration guide for partners describing header semantics and how to opt out.
technical_notes: Design summary: build a three-stage resolver pipeline: 1) fast alias lookup (exact matches + canonicalization: casing, underscores/dashes), 2) fuzzy match with signature scoring (Levenshtein + tokenized name similarity + parameter set overlap), 3) schema-aware coercion (JSON Schema soft coercion with explicit warnings). Each decision produces a confidence score between 0.0-1.0 and a provenance string (e.g., 'alias:email_v1->legacy_send_email;method:alias_lookup;reason:exact_case_insensitive'). Expose mapping metadata to callers via response metadata (x-rw-tool-confidence, x-rw-tool-provenance) and to internal telemetry events. Avoid automatic destructive coercions: if coercion would drop fields or change numeric types with potential precision loss, mark as low-confidence and surface to logs. Persist alias table in runtime-config store with fast in-memory refresh and versioning. For streaming, mapping metadata is emitted as the first tool-call event in the stream and tagged on subsequent chunks for traceability.
implementation_plan: Week 1: implement alias lookup engine and in-memory table format + config API for Console to manage aliases.
Week 2: add fuzzy matcher and signature scorer; unit tests for common name/param permutations.
Week 3: implement JSON schema-aware coercion module and streaming metadata hooks; integrate with runtime event stream.
Week 4: add telemetry + dashboards; create toggle mechanism (per-customer and per-route); write canary rollout script.
Week 5: e2e testing with Dedicated and Private environments, partner migration playbook, documentation and SDK examples.
progress_updates: 2025-03-01: RFC posted. Initial design reviewed by Runtime and SDK teams. Decision: resolver lives in request routing layer, not model layer.
2025-03-03: Alias table proto implemented; Console API stub created. Running microbenchmarks; alias lookup median 0.3ms.
2025-03-06: Fuzzy scorer prototype checked in (python harness). Early tests show 87% precision on internal signal set; need to improve recall for camelCase variants.
2025-03-10: Streaming hook implemented; metadata is emitted as first tool-call event in local integration harness. Preparing canary plan for 5% traffic on staging.
